mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕跨文化沟通展开，涵盖有效的跨文化沟通（Reading）、融入异国文化（Extended reading）、尊重与包容文化差异（Grammar and usage）和在交流中开阔视野（Integrated skills）四个板块——跨文化交流是高考应用文'书信/发言'类的常见场景，也是雅思语言与全球化类议论文的高频命题。

subTopics.title: 有效的跨文化沟通
subTopics.desc: 课文核心：面对偏爱直接风格的美国人，作者常常 failed to get the message across；good communication skills will help you build trust and gain respect——沟通的关键，是读懂彼此的风格与情感。

prompts.task: 你校将迎来一批外国交换生。请你用英文写一篇短文投稿校刊，谈谈如何与来自不同文化的人有效沟通，内容包括：1. 沟通中可能的误解；2. 你的两三条建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Next month, a group of exchange students will join our school, and getting along with them may not always be as easy as it looks.

People from different cultures often communicate differently. Some, like many Americans, have a preference for a direct style, while others express themselves more gently and indirectly. Without care, we may fail to get the message across, or even give offence without meaning to.

So how can we communicate well? First, listen with empathy and try to understand the feelings behind the words. Second, ask politely instead of guessing when something is unclear. Above all, be sincere. Good communication skills help us build trust and gain respect — and turn strangers into friends.
vocabHints: a preference for a direct style
fail to get the message across

prompts.task: Some people believe that good communication skills are more important for success than academic knowledge. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Schools reward examination results, yet many argue that the ability to communicate matters more to success in life than academic knowledge. I partly agree: communication skills are indispensable and often decisive, but they work best built upon real knowledge rather than in place of it.

The case for communication is strong. Most achievements depend on other people — persuading them, leading them, cooperating with them — and none of this is possible without the ability to express ideas clearly and to listen with empathy. A brilliant engineer who cannot explain a design, or a researcher who cannot present findings, sees good work ignored. In workplaces, promotions frequently go to those who communicate well, and the ability to build trust and resolve conflict shapes careers as powerfully as any qualification.

However, communication without substance is empty. A speaker who charms but knows nothing may succeed briefly, yet is soon exposed; expertise, technical skill and sound judgement remain the foundation on which persuasion rests. In medicine, law or science, no amount of eloquence compensates for not knowing the facts. The two, moreover, reinforce each other: knowledge gives one something worth communicating, while communication turns private knowledge into shared value.

The realistic conclusion is that neither alone suffices. Academic learning provides the content; communication delivers it to the world, and success usually requires both.

In conclusion, while I agree that communication skills are enormously important — often the difference between talent recognised and talent wasted — they cannot replace knowledge. The most successful people are those who both understand deeply and express clearly.

subTopics.title: 尊重与包容文化差异
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：have a preference for、be tolerant of、behave differently、correspond to——面对文化差异，理解'不同'不等于'错误'，是包容的第一步。

prompts.task: 你班就'如何看待中外文化差异'开展讨论。请你用英文写一篇短文，谈谈你的看法，内容包括：1. 举一个文化差异的例子；2. 你主张的态度。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
During our exchange week, I noticed that my German friend always said exactly what she thought, while I tended to soften my words. At first this felt rude — until I realised it was simply a different style.

Different cultures have different preferences, and what seems impolite in one may be perfectly normal in another. A direct "no" does not correspond to unfriendliness; it is just another way of being honest. Rather than judging, we should be tolerant of these differences and try to understand why people behave as they do.

Difference is not the same as wrong. When we meet another culture with curiosity instead of judgement, misunderstanding gives way to respect, and the world grows a little wider.
vocabHints: why people behave as they do
difference is not the same as wrong

prompts.task: Some people believe that living or studying in a foreign country makes people more tolerant of cultural differences. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
It is often assumed that spending time abroad broadens the mind and makes people more accepting of other cultures. I largely agree, though I would add that tolerance grows only when the experience is approached with an open attitude.

The main reason living abroad increases tolerance is direct contact. Reading about another culture is not the same as living inside it: when someone eats unfamiliar food daily, follows local customs and forms friendships across a cultural line, the stereotypes that distance preserves quietly dissolve. Behaviour that once seemed strange starts to make sense once its reasons are understood, and people learn that different does not mean wrong. Facing the discomfort of being a foreigner oneself, moreover, teaches a lasting sympathy for outsiders everywhere.

Nevertheless, exposure alone guarantees nothing. Some who live abroad mix only with people from their own country, judge everything by the standards of home, and return more prejudiced than before, their worst assumptions apparently confirmed. Tolerance depends less on physical distance travelled than on willingness to engage — to be curious rather than defensive, and to accept that one's own way is not the only correct one.

On balance, therefore, living abroad usually does make people more tolerant, because sustained real contact is the most powerful cure for prejudice. But the effect is not automatic; it rewards those who arrive ready to learn.

In conclusion, while a foreign experience is not a magic guarantee of open-mindedness, for most people who embrace it genuinely, it deepens tolerance in a way no book or lecture can match.

subTopics.title: 在交流中开阔视野
subTopics.desc: 综合技能板块核心词块：expand one's horizons、gain a new perspective、become more open-minded——每一次跨文化的交流，都是给心灵开一扇新的窗。

prompts.task: 你校组织了一次中外学生文化交流活动，你参加后收获很大。请你用英文为校英文报写一篇短文，内容包括：1. 活动内容；2. 你的收获与感悟。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Last weekend I joined a culture exchange event with students from five countries, and it opened my eyes in ways I did not expect.

We shared songs, food and stories from our hometowns. When I recited a Chinese poem, a British student surprised us all by reciting one too — without an accent! Hearing how differently we each saw the same world, I felt my horizons expand hour by hour.

What I gained was more than fun. Talking with people so unlike me helped me gain a new perspective and become more open-minded. I came home realising that our differences are not walls but windows. I can't wait for the next exchange — the world, it turns out, is far bigger and warmer than my classroom.

prompts.task: Some people think that studying abroad is the best way for young people to broaden their horizons, while others believe this can be achieved just as well at home. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Broadening one's horizons is a widely shared goal, but people disagree on how best to achieve it. Some insist that studying abroad is unmatched; others argue that an open mind can be developed without leaving home. Having weighed both, I believe studying abroad offers uniquely powerful experiences, yet a curious person can grow greatly at home as well.

The case for going abroad is compelling. Living in another country immerses a young person completely: they must manage daily life in a foreign language, adapt to unfamiliar customs and see their own country through outsiders' eyes. This total immersion builds independence, empathy and a new perspective far faster than occasional contact can, and the friendships formed leave lasting impressions no textbook could.

However, studying abroad is expensive and out of reach for many, and it is not the only road to a wider mind. A student at home can read world literature, learn languages, join international online communities, attend cultural events and befriend people from other backgrounds. Curiosity, not a plane ticket, is what truly broadens the mind; without it, even a year overseas teaches little, while with it, one's own city becomes a classroom.

My own view is that studying abroad, where possible, provides the richest and quickest growth, but it is a privilege rather than a necessity. The essential ingredient is an open, questioning attitude, which can be cultivated anywhere.

In conclusion, while a period abroad is an extraordinary way to broaden horizons, it is not the only way. What matters most is the willingness to seek out the unfamiliar, wherever one happens to be.

subTopics.title: 融入异国文化
subTopics.desc: 拓展阅读核心：It's very difficult to integrate yourself into a society whose culture is so different from your own——融入不是丢掉自己，而是在真诚与尊重中，找到与新环境相处的方式。

prompts.task: 你的朋友 Mike 即将到中国留学，担心难以适应。请你用英文回信，给他一些融入中国生活的建议，内容包括：1. 表达理解；2. 两三条建议；3. 鼓励。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Mike,

I'm so glad you're coming to study in China! It's natural to worry, because it is never easy to integrate yourself into a society whose culture is so different from your own.

Here are a few tips. First, learn some basic Chinese — even a sincere "nihao" opens doors. Second, don't be afraid to make mistakes; when you slip up, apologise sincerely and people will warm to you. Third, say yes to invitations, share meals, and ask about customs instead of guessing. Little by little, the strange becomes familiar.

You won't lose who you are by fitting in; you'll simply grow bigger. I can't wait to show you around. See you soon!

Yours,
Li Hua

prompts.task: When people move to live in a new country, some think they should adapt to the local culture, while others believe they should keep their own culture and traditions. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
As migration increases, newcomers face a delicate question: should they blend into the local culture, or preserve the traditions they bring with them? Some urge full adaptation; others defend cultural continuity. In my view the two are not opposites, and the healthiest path combines respect for the host society with pride in one's own heritage.

The argument for adapting is practical and considerate. Immigrants who learn the local language, follow local customs and understand local values integrate far more easily — they find work, make friends and avoid the isolation that traps those who remain apart. Adapting also shows respect for the community that has received them, and eases the tensions that unfamiliarity can breed.

Yet demanding that newcomers erase their own culture is neither fair nor wise. A person's language, food, festivals and beliefs are part of who they are, and abandoning them causes real loss and rootlessness. Diversity, moreover, enriches the host society itself: the most vibrant cities draw energy precisely from the many cultures that meet within them. A migrant who keeps their heritage while embracing their new home offers the best of both.

The sensible balance, therefore, is integration without erasure. Newcomers should learn the local ways enough to participate fully, while keeping the traditions that give their lives meaning, and host societies should welcome that blend rather than demand uniformity.

In conclusion, adapting to a new country and preserving one's own culture are not contradictory but complementary. The most successful immigrants, and the most successful societies, are those that manage to hold both at once.
